title: Kinesthetic Involvement

outline.heading: Macro Phase: Agency
outline.summary: Establishes ergodic engagement as the precondition of the kinesthetic dimension and develops a multi-source definition of agency. Murray's 'satisfying power to take meaningful action' is qualified by counter-cases (a Counter-Strike grenade misfiring onto teammates); Mateas + Stern's local/global distinction is introduced; Calleja then settles on Giddens's capability-based agency (acting otherwise, not intention) to make room for unintended and persistent MMOG consequences. Malaby's contrivance-of-contingency reframes games as systems calibrating predictable and unpredictable outcomes, with failure intrinsic to performance.

outline.heading: Micro Phase: In-Game Control (unnamed transitional paragraph)
outline.summary: Pivots from generalized agency to moment-to-moment in-game control. Introduces the avatar-vs-miniatures distinction: the avatar is the single entity in which player presence is fixed; miniatures are entities the player controls without those entities representing the player. Examples: cavalry units (Medieval II), workers (Age of Empires), falling blocks (Tetris).

outline.heading: Modes of Control in Game Environments
outline.summary: Differentiates single-miniature, simultaneous-miniature, single-avatar, and hybrid avatar/miniature schemes. Tetris exemplifies single-miniature focus interleaving kinesthetic / ludic / spatial sub-attention; Empire: Total War exemplifies simultaneous multi-unit command. Avatar control consolidates attention on one entity (Pong's pixel bar still counts because it is the locus of agency). FIFA 2009 illustrates oscillation between miniature-management and single-avatar focus.

outline.heading: Modes of Game Control
outline.summary: Introduces the chapter's central typology: a continuum from symbolic (keys/buttons/thumb sticks with no mimetic relation to avatar action) through mimetic (partial mapping — Wii Sports, Grand Slam Tennis, light guns, steering wheels) to symbiotic (Kinect / Project Natal — full-body capture aimed at eliminating the controller altogether). Visualized in Figure 4.3 ('Forms of control in digital games'). Calleja notes a market-driven shift toward symbiotic control to recruit casual and older players. Hybrid combinations (No More Heroes, Wii Sports baseball) acknowledge that some functions — spatial navigation especially — resist mimetic translation.

outline.heading: Kinesthetic Pleasure
outline.summary: Begins with a brief genealogy of movement-affordance (Space Invaders' single axis, Pacman's plane, Max Payne's full repertoire plus bullet-time). Argues that bullet-time games (Max Payne, Enter the Matrix, F.E.A.R.) externalize media-imported fantasies of motion. Treats first-person presence (the keystroke felt as one's own forward jump) and third-person 'double awareness'. Identifies internalization of controls as the pleasure peak: participant vocabularies 'Quan' (Bladerunner) and 'flow' (Sunniva, vernacular use, NOT Csikszentmihalyi-cited) name this disappearance-of-mediation. Sue Morris (2002) supplies the chapter's only academic anchor for the 'thinking with the fingers' / player-as-extension thesis. Mirror's Edge is the paradigmatic case of designed continuity-of-movement; obstacles are recoded (generically, without Gibson attribution) as 'affordances' for fluid motion. The chapter then contests Melanie Swalwell's (2008) LAN-party kinesthetic research for conflating onlooker and player experience: only the player is inside the player-game circuit and bears the failures and accomplishments of control. The Red Orchestra sniper-waiting passage (cross-cited to chapter 3) recasts kinesthetic involvement as a disposition to act — readiness — not the discrete keystroke. The unnamed closing coda (book pp.71-72) ties kinesthetic fluency to the other PIM dimensions: movement is foundational because other forms of involvement depend on basic environmental fluency.

dimension_operational_definition: Kinesthetic involvement is the player's experience of exerting agency through control and movement of avatars and miniatures within a virtual environment, indexed across a macro phase (general capability to act on the game world, in the Giddens-inflected sense of acting-otherwise under designed contingency) and a micro phase (moment-to-moment in-game control whose modes range across a symbolic / mimetic / symbiotic continuum and whose pleasure peaks in the internalization-of-controls that lets movement be felt as unmediated).

boundary_criteria.criterion: Kinesthetic involvement is registered when attention is on actions producing motion of an avatar or miniatures (key-press / thumb-stick / body-capture). When attention shifts to goal-structures and rule-pursuit, ludic involvement is foregrounded; when it shifts to environmental orientation, spatial involvement is foregrounded.
boundary_criteria.evidence_source: Tetris worked example (Calleja interleaves kinesthetic with ludic and spatial sub-attention on the same play episode), book p.60

boundary_criteria.criterion: All other dimensions presuppose basic kinesthetic fluency: a player who cannot reliably move cannot inhabit space (spatial), pursue goals (ludic), coordinate with co-players (shared), follow scripted-or-emergent narrative arcs (narrative), or undergo gameplay-elicited affect (affective). Kinesthetic is the foundational layer.

Kinesthetic involvement is ergodic (player-internal to the player-game circuit); the onlooker's sympathetic excitation, however vivid, is mimetic-only and is misclassified if treated as equivalent to player kinesthetic experience.

Control-scheme position on the symbolic→mimetic→symbiotic continuum is a discriminating feature of the kinesthetic dimension. Symbolic control (FPS WASD) prioritizes encoded dexterity; mimetic control (Wii) prioritizes partial body-mapping; symbiotic control (Kinect) prioritizes full body-capture. Spatial / ludic / narrative dimensions do not vary along this continuum.
boundary_criteria.evidence_source: Figure 4.3 and surrounding analysis, book pp.63-65

boundary_criteria.criterion: Mature kinesthetic involvement produces a phenomenological signature — the controls 'disappear', the player feels the action as her own ('Quan'; 'thinking with fingers'; 'I am now flying'; 'it's me'). This signature does not arise in spatial, ludic, narrative, affective, or shared involvement in the same form.
boundary_criteria.evidence_source: Bladerunner / Morris / Evita passages, book pp.66-68

boundary_criteria.criterion: Kinesthetic involvement includes anticipatory readiness, not only realized input. A sniper waiting motionless is still kinesthetically involved if she is tense with anticipation to move-aim-fire at the kairotic moment. Spatial involvement, by contrast, is about being-in-the-environment regardless of intent-to-move.
boundary_criteria.evidence_source: Red Orchestra sniper passage, book p.70

concepts.label: Kinesthetic involvement
concepts.definition: Player exertion of agency through control and movement; one of the six PIM dimensions.

concepts.label: Agency (Murray-Schott sense)
concepts.definition: Satisfying power to take meaningful action and see the results; foundational engagement contributor.

concepts.label: Local agency (Mateas + Stern)
concepts.definition: Player ability to see immediate reactions to her interaction.

concepts.label: Global agency (Mateas + Stern)
concepts.definition: Knowledge of longer-term consequences along a causal chain.

concepts.label: Agency-as-capability (Giddens)
concepts.definition: Calleja's preferred reframing: agency is capability of doing things (acting otherwise), not intention. Decouples agency from satisfaction and from knowledge of consequences.

concepts.label: Contrivance of contingency (Malaby)
concepts.definition: Games as processes that design unpredictable circumstances admitting meaningful, culturally shared, open-ended interpretation; rules differ from everyday-life rules in calibrating rather than reducing unpredictability.

concepts.label: Performance and risk of failure
concepts.definition: Action that may succeed or fail; performative under contingency; intrinsic to athletic and FPS contests.

concepts.label: Skill-vs-attribute modulation
concepts.definition: Designed variation in how player ability is mediated by avatar attributes (none in Counter-Strike; heavy in Oblivion / WoW; intermediate in Planetside).

concepts.label: Avatar control
concepts.definition: Player presence fixed in a single entity (first- or third-person); the most intimate player-entity link via movement.

concepts.label: Miniature control
concepts.definition: Player manipulation of entities that do not represent the player; player occupies an external / omniscient position.

concepts.label: Individual vs simultaneous miniature control
concepts.definition: Tetris (one block at a time) vs Empire: Total War (up to twenty multi-miniature units commanded together).

concepts.label: Avatar / miniature oscillation
concepts.definition: Hybrid scheme (FIFA 2009): control vests in one active player at a time while simultaneously directing formation and assisting players.

concepts.label: Symbolic control
concepts.definition: Keys, buttons, thumb sticks; no mimetic relation between player motion and avatar motion.

concepts.label: Mimetic control
concepts.definition: Partial mapping of player motion onto avatar motion (Wii Sports, Grand Slam Tennis, light guns, steering wheels).

concepts.label: Symbiotic control
concepts.definition: Full body-capture (Kinect / Project Natal); aims to eliminate the controller altogether; facial / vocal / proximity recognition included.

concepts.label: Symbolic ↔ symbiotic continuum (Figure 4.3 typology)
concepts.definition: Calleja's primary analytic innovation in this chapter — a one-dimensional scale of control-scheme intimacy that explains the casual-gamer market shift and the design rationale for body-capture platforms.

concepts.label: Hybrid control modes
concepts.definition: Combination schemes (e.g. No More Heroes' nunchuk-stick navigation plus Wii-mote action swings; Wii Sports baseball's mimetic-pitch + symbolic-pitch-type). Necessary because some functions (spatial navigation especially) resist mimetic translation.

concepts.label: Double awareness in third-person perspective
concepts.definition: Simultaneous awareness of camera-portrayed surroundings and of space-as-related-to-avatar; first/third-person switching forces re-anchoring of line-of-sight.

concepts.label: Bullet-time / fantasy of movement
concepts.definition: Designed exception to ordinary kinematics enabling Neo-like maneuvers; partly realizes internal imagery imported from cinema (Max Payne, Enter the Matrix, F.E.A.R.).

concepts.label: Internalization of controls ('Quan'; thinking with fingers)
concepts.definition: Mastery state in which on-screen movement feels unmediated and willed; Bladerunner's vernacular 'Quan' (from the film Jerry Maguire), Morris's 'think with their fingers', Evita's 'it's me' all name this signature.

concepts.label: Player-as-extension-of-game / game-as-extension-of-player
concepts.definition: Morris's two-way framing of the mature kinesthetic circuit, cited approvingly by Calleja as describing FPS mastery.

concepts.label: Disposition to act / anticipatory readiness
concepts.definition: The active intention to perform the action at the kairotic moment, not merely the realized input; the Red Orchestra sniper waiting is kinesthetically involved.

concepts.label: Continuity of movement
concepts.definition: Designed reward structure (Mirror's Edge) for sustaining momentum, perfect timing, and uninterrupted flow through an obstacle field; parkour inspiration.

concepts.label: Kinesthetic pleasure
concepts.definition: Movement-as-enjoyable-in-its-own-right once controls are mastered; the gateway to fluent engagement with the environment.

concepts.label: Ergodic vs mimetic kinesthetic experience
concepts.definition: The player is inside the player-game circuit (ergodic + mimetic); the onlooker is restricted to the mimetic register and cannot bear the failures or accomplishments of control.

concepts.label: Movement as foundational across PIM
concepts.definition: Closing thesis: other dimensions depend on basic environmental fluency; kinesthetic is the substrate.

concepts.label: Affordances for movement (generic, NOT Gibson-cited)
concepts.definition: Designed environmental features that solicit fluid motion (Mirror's Edge parkour). Calleja uses the word once at p.69 without Gibson attribution — the chapter's affordance-talk is theoretically thin (cite_check.gibson verdict).

concepts.label: 'Flow' (Sunniva participant-vernacular, NOT Csikszentmihalyi-cited)
concepts.definition: Participant-coined description of 'continuous focus' likened to surfing. Calleja preserves the participant's word; cite_check confirms zero Csikszentmihalyi engagement in the volume.

positions.label: Capability over satisfaction: Giddens's agency displaces Murray's
positions.claim: Calleja preferentially defines agency as capability-to-act-otherwise (Giddens 1984), not as intention or satisfaction, in order to keep unintended and persistent consequences inside the kinesthetic dimension.

positions.label: Contingency is constitutive of games, not incidental
positions.claim: Following Malaby (2007), games are systems that calibrate contingency rather than reduce it; failure is intrinsic, and 'too well learned' games (tic-tac-toe) cease to be games.

positions.label: Symbolic / mimetic / symbiotic continuum as the chapter's primary typology
positions.claim: Forms of control vary along a single continuum (Figure 4.3); the industry's market-driven trajectory is toward the symbiotic pole because that pole recruits casual-gamer and older demographics.

positions.label: Player ≠ onlooker kinesthetically
positions.claim: Against Swalwell (2008), only the player is inside the game-player circuit and bears the agency-attached failures and accomplishments; sympathetic onlooker excitation is mimetic-only and is misclassified if treated as kinesthetically equivalent.

positions.label: Kinesthetic involvement is the substrate of the other dimensions
positions.claim: Most other forms of involvement depend on developing at least basic fluency of movement in the environment — kinesthetic is foundational, not coordinate.

positions.label: Anticipatory readiness extends the kinesthetic register
positions.claim: Kinesthetic involvement includes the disposition to act (readiness, kairotic anticipation), not only the discrete input; the waiting sniper is kinesthetically involved.

tensions.label: Murray's intention-satisfaction agency vs Giddens's capability agency
tensions.summary: Murray's account ties agency to satisfaction of intended outcomes; Calleja's worked example (the misfired Counter-Strike grenade) shows agency can be exerted with neither intended nor satisfying results. Giddens supplies the broader frame. The two definitions remain partially incommensurable — Calleja preserves Murray's vocabulary while supplanting her semantics.

tensions.label: Industry shift to symbiotic vs persistence of symbolic in core gameplay
tensions.summary: Calleja documents a market-driven shift toward symbiotic (Kinect) control while also noting that spatial navigation resists mimetic translation and that hybrid schemes persist precisely because some functions cannot be mimetically rendered. The continuum is therefore not unidirectional — it has zones of irreducible asymmetry that the typology itself does not fully theorize.

tensions.label: Calleja's ergodic-only kinesthesia vs Swalwell's player-and-onlooker register
tensions.summary: Swalwell's LAN-party research treats onlooker excitation as a kinesthetic register; Calleja restricts kinesthetic involvement to those inside the player-game agency-circuit. This is a substantive disciplinary contest, not a terminological adjustment — it draws the line of what counts as kinesthesia.

game_loci.title: Counter-Strike: Source
game_loci.analytic_role: Worked example for agency-with-unintended-outcomes (lobbed grenade kills teammates); illustrates skill-without-attribute-modulation (avatar attributes irrelevant to player ability).

game_loci.title: Planetside
game_loci.analytic_role: Persistent-MMOG exemplar for Giddens-style agency (mines laid that may decide a battle without the player present); dexterity-over-level skill paradigm; supplies most participant quotes (Evita, Kestra, Baal, Sunniva, Bladerunner, BunkerBoy86).

game_loci.title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion
game_loci.analytic_role: Heavy attribute-modulation case: numeric character stats modify player success; time-invested skill enhancement raises sense of agency beyond the game world.

game_loci.title: World of Warcraft
game_loci.analytic_role: Twenty-level gap means even maximum player skill cannot win — attribute-dominant agency case; also closing example of leisurely-mount-traversal as a kinesthetic-aesthetic pleasure.

game_loci.title: Medieval II: Total War
game_loci.analytic_role: Miniature example: cavalry units as entities that do not represent the player.

game_loci.title: Age of Empires
game_loci.analytic_role: Miniature example: workers as controlled non-self entities.

game_loci.title: Tetris
game_loci.analytic_role: Single-miniature paradigm; demonstrates kinesthetic / ludic / spatial sub-attention interleaving within one play episode.

game_loci.title: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War
game_loci.analytic_role: RTS exemplar of roving-point-of-view control not anchored to a single avatar.

game_loci.title: Empire: Total War
game_loci.analytic_role: Simultaneous-miniature paradigm: up to twenty multi-miniature units commanded as whole, group, or individual; Figure 4.1 anchor.

game_loci.title: FIFA 2009
game_loci.analytic_role: Avatar-miniature oscillation paradigm; player-run function and tackle-button assist demonstrate that attention can split between active-player control and team-formation management; Figure 4.2 anchor.

game_loci.title: Pong
game_loci.analytic_role: Limit-case for avatar control: even a vertical bar of pixels is an avatar if it is the locus of agency exertion.

game_loci.title: Wii Sports
game_loci.analytic_role: Paradigm of mimetic control: Wii-mote tennis swing maps onto on-screen avatar swing; boxing wholly mimetic, baseball hybrid (mimetic pitch + symbolic pitch-type).

game_loci.title: Grand Slam Tennis
game_loci.analytic_role: Mimetic control example alongside Wii Sports.

game_loci.title: The House of the Dead
game_loci.analytic_role: Light-gun arcade rail-shooter; controller-replicates-tool form of mimetic control.

game_loci.title: No More Heroes
game_loci.analytic_role: Hybrid paradigm: thumb-stick navigation plus Wii-mote action swings; demonstrates that spatial navigation resists mimetic translation.

game_loci.title: Kinect / Project Natal (platform: Xbox 360)
game_loci.analytic_role: Paradigm of symbiotic control: full-body capture, facial/voice/distance recognition; eliminate-the-controller design ambition; market-recruitment vehicle for casual / older / cross-gender demographics.

game_loci.title: Wii / Wii-mote (platform)
game_loci.analytic_role: Platform-level paradigm of mimetic control; market success for older / cross-generational demographic underwrites the symbolic→symbiotic shift argument.

game_loci.title: Space Invaders
game_loci.analytic_role: Movement-affordance genealogy: single-axis motion (left/right plus vertical fire).

game_loci.title: Pacman
game_loci.analytic_role: Movement-affordance genealogy: four-direction motion on a plane.

game_loci.title: Max Payne
game_loci.analytic_role: Bullet-time paradigm: walk / crouch / sprint / jump while aim-shooting plus slowed-action regime; externalization of cinema-imported fantasies of motion (Neo-like speed). Figure 4.4 anchor.

game_loci.title: Enter the Matrix
game_loci.analytic_role: Bullet-time / Matrix-fantasy realization.

game_loci.title: F.E.A.R.
game_loci.analytic_role: Bullet-time / Matrix-fantasy realization.

game_loci.title: The Matrix Online
game_loci.analytic_role: Cited via Baal's participant quote on 'mega hyperjumps' between buildings as a kinesthetic-pleasure exemplar.

game_loci.title: Mirror's Edge
game_loci.analytic_role: Paradigm of designed continuity-of-movement: parkour-inspired, reward structure for perfect-timing momentum; obstacle field recoded (generically) as 'affordances' for fluid motion. Figure 4.5 anchor. THEORETICALLY THIN affordance-talk — no Gibson attribution.

game_loci.title: Red Orchestra
game_loci.analytic_role: Disposition-to-act paradigm: motionless waiting sniper as kinesthetically involved via anticipatory readiness; cross-cited from chapter 3.

interlocutors.name: Janet H. Murray
interlocutors.role: Foundational agency-as-satisfying-power citation; Calleja preserves vocabulary but supplants semantics.

interlocutors.name: Gareth Schott
interlocutors.role: Subjective experience of agency as prime engagement contributor.

interlocutors.name: Michael Mateas and Andrew Stern
interlocutors.role: Local vs global agency distinction; intention + action + interpretation triad.

interlocutors.name: Anthony Giddens
interlocutors.role: Capability-not-intention reframing; supplies Calleja's preferred agency definition.

interlocutors.name: Thomas Malaby
interlocutors.role: Contrivance of contingency; calibration not reduction; performance-and-risk-of-failure framing.

interlocutors.name: Sue Morris
interlocutors.role: Internalization of controls — 'think with their fingers' — player-as-extension framing; sole academic anchor for the kinesthetic-pleasure thesis.

interlocutors.name: Melanie Swalwell
interlocutors.role: Critical foil — Calleja faults her for conflating onlooker and player kinesthetic experience.

interlocutors.name: Van Rooyen-McLeay
interlocutors.role: Cited via Swalwell — physical-excitation observation at arcade machines (onlooker leg-twitching).

interlocutors.name: Wachowski and Wachowski (dirs.)
interlocutors.role: Cinema-import: source of the slow-motion-acrobatics imagery that bullet-time games externalize.

interlocutors.name: Bladerunner (Planetside participant)
interlocutors.role: Coiner of 'Quan' (vernacular borrowed from the film Jerry Maguire) for the internalized-control signature; NOT promoted to canonical concept but tracked as vivid participant vocabulary.

interlocutors.name: Sunniva (Planetside participant)
interlocutors.role: Vernacular use of 'flow' / 'continuous focus' / 'wave' / 'surfing' simile to describe continuity-of-movement experience. NOT Csikszentmihalyi-cited.

interlocutors.name: Evita (Planetside participant)
interlocutors.role: Articulates Malaby's contingency thesis ('freedom to act'); supplies the closing 'it's me' quote on identification with the avatar.

interlocutors.name: Baal (Planetside participant)
interlocutors.role: Bullet-time / Matrix-Online 'mega hyperjumps' and 'really holding that gun' quotes anchor the kinesthetic-pleasure passages.

paradigm_worked_examples.analytic_move: Used in macro-phase exposition to dissociate agency from satisfaction and intention: the player's grenade-throw is an unambiguous exertion of agency even though it produces an unintended outcome (his teammates die). The example carries the Giddens-over-Murray argument.

Used to illustrate single-miniature focus and the way one play episode interleaves three PIM dimensions in micro succession: rotating the falling block (kinesthetic), monitoring the upcoming block (ludic), and clearing layers to control the game space (spatial). Demonstrates that miniature control does not preclude multi-dimensional attention.

Paradigm of simultaneous-miniature command: up to twenty multi-miniature units issued orders as whole, sub-groups, or individual units. Figure 4.1 anchor. Shows that the kinesthetic dimension scales to commander-level distributed attention without ceasing to be kinesthetic.

Paradigm of avatar / miniature oscillation: control vests in one active player at a time but the player-run and tackle-assist functions extend attention to formation and to inactive teammates. Figure 4.2 anchor. Shows the avatar / miniature distinction is not always categorical.

Paradigm of mimetic control: the Wii-mote tennis-swing maps onto the on-screen avatar's swing, expanding the kinesthetic dimension to account for the player's bodily performance. The baseball-game hybrid (mimetic pitch + symbolic pitch-type) shows that mimetic and symbolic modes co-exist within a single title.

Paradigm of symbiotic control: full-body capture with facial / voice / proximity recognition; design ambition is to eliminate the controller. Carries the market-shift argument — symbiotic recruitment of casual / older / cross-gender demographics — that anchors the symbolic→symbiotic continuum claim.

Paradigm of bullet-time / fantasy-realization: full walk/crouch/sprint/jump repertoire plus slowed-action regime externalizes the cinema-imported Neo-fantasy. Used to argue that some kinesthetic pleasure depends on designed exceptions to ordinary kinematics; Figure 4.4 anchor.

Paradigm of continuity-of-movement: parkour-inspired reward structure for perfect-timing momentum recodes obstacles as (generic, non-Gibson) 'affordances' for fluid motion. The strongest single illustration of the chapter's closing thesis that movement-fluency is the pleasure peak of kinesthetic involvement; Figure 4.5 anchor.

burke_pentad.rationale: The chapter's whole expository thrust — exertion of agency through control and movement — is structurally aligned with Burke's Agency pentad-term (the means / instruments of action). The symbolic / mimetic / symbiotic continuum is a typology of Agency (in Burke's pentadal sense). Secondary: Calleja's player-as-extension framing (Morris cited) parallels Burke's consubstantiation / identification — the rhetorical figure by which actor and instrument become one substance. This is the cleanest pentad mapping in the volume.
burke_pentad.exegetical_anchor_in_calleja: NONE — cite_check confirms zero Burke engagement in the text, references, or index.

uexkull_construct.rationale: The player-avatar feedback loop (key-press → avatar response → perceptual feedback → next key-press), thematized most explicitly in the Morris 'think with their fingers' passage and the Bladerunner 'Quan' framing, is structurally identical to Uexküll's perception-action functional cycle (Merkmal → Merkorgan → Innenwelt → Wirkorgan → Wirkmal). Secondary: the symbolic / mimetic / symbiotic continuum can be read as varying tightness of Merkorgan-Wirkorgan coupling — symbolic = loose coupling via encoded mediation, mimetic = partial body-mapped coupling, symbiotic = maximally tight body-mapped coupling.
uexkull_construct.exegetical_anchor_in_calleja: NONE — cite_check confirms zero Uexküll engagement; the Gibson-mediation hypothesis is FALSIFIED (Calleja's one 'affordance' use at p.69 is generic / non-Gibson).

ontological_grounding_aristotelian_heide.term: aisthesis-kinesis + dunamis/hexis via Bowin AMT; kairotic readiness via Heidegger BCAP
ontological_grounding_aristotelian_heide.rationale: STRONGEST CHAPTER FOR THIS ANCHOR. (1) IG-03's ergodicity-as-disposition framing (propagated finding) pre-figures Aristotelian dunamis (potency) / hexis (settled disposition) without the vocabulary — IG-04's 'disposition to act' (Red Orchestra sniper) and the internalization-of-controls passages are the textual sites where dunamis-actualized-as-energeia receives its clearest pre-figuration: kinesthetic involvement is readiness-to-act actualized through skill-acquired hexis. (2) The continuity-of-motion analysis (Sunniva's 'continuous motion'; Mirror's Edge as 'continuity of movement') is the paradigm Bowin AMT (Aristotelian Motion and Time) bridge target — Bowin's aisthesis-kinesis treatment supplies the ontological vocabulary the chapter lacks. (3) The waiting-sniper passage's kairotic anticipation bridges to Heidegger BCAP analyses of kairos and anticipatory comportment.
ontological_grounding_aristotelian_heide.exegetical_anchor_in_calleja: NONE — cite_check confirms zero Aristotle, zero Merleau-Ponty; one Heidegger cite at p.21 (Question Concerning Technology) outside this chapter.

residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.phenomenological_register_language: the player feels like an extension of the game or the game feels like an extension of the player
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.layer_A_anchor_target: Heideggerian zuhanden / equipment-totality (BCAP); Bowin AMT hexis; potential Merleau-Pontian body-schema target (not in current corpus)
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.note: Direct paraphrase of Morris (2002, p.85) — Calleja cites Morris but Morris herself does not invoke phenomenology. The 'extension' language is the residual phenomenology-without-phenomenologist.

residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.phenomenological_register_language: your mind is willing those actions
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.layer_A_anchor_target: Aristotelian boulesis / orexis-cum-energeia via Bowin AMT; potential Husserlian I-can / kinesthetic-sensation target (not in current corpus)
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.note: Participant-vernacular but Calleja preserves it because it names the unmediated-willed-action signature. Strong Layer-A candidate.

residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.phenomenological_register_language: continuous motion that keeps my attention on the game ... a certain steady, continuous focus
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.layer_A_anchor_target: Bowin AMT continuity-of-motion analysis; Heideggerian ekstatic temporality (BCAP)
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.note: Participant uses 'flow' vernacularly — NOT Csikszentmihalyi-cited. The temporal continuity language is the residual phenomenology.

residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.phenomenological_register_language: Thumbing the space key and pressing W in an FPS is most often interpreted by the player as a forward jump they have made, rather than as the forward jump of a character they control ... I am now flying an aircraft ... it's me
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.layer_A_anchor_target: Merleau-Pontian body-schema extension; Heideggerian In-der-Welt-sein via mediated equipment (BCAP analogue); body-as-mine / Leib-Körper
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.note: Strongest residual-phenomenology site in the chapter. The 'mineness' of avatar-action is described phenomenologically without any phenomenologist cited.

residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.phenomenological_register_language: tense with anticipation to move the crosshairs, lead the target, hold her breath ... the active intention to perform the action at the right time ... the expectation of performance can be just as engaging as the performance itself
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.layer_A_anchor_target: Heideggerian kairotic readiness / anticipatory comportment (BCAP); Aristotelian hexis-as-readiness via Bowin AMT

cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: Continuity-of-motion analysis (Mirror's Edge, Sunniva), dunamis/hexis pre-figuration via 'disposition to act', and kinesthetic-pleasure-as-actualized-readiness all converge on Bowin's aisthesis-kinesis treatment.
Kairotic readiness via Red Orchestra sniper; zuhanden / equipment-totality via Morris 'thinking with fingers'; In-der-Welt-sein analogue via Evita 'it's me'.
Funktionskreis as player-avatar feedback loop; symbolic/mimetic/symbiotic continuum as variable Merkorgan-Wirkorgan coupling tightness.
